findings.title: GPU inference is faster on every board with Mesa 25.2.8 and the TensorFlow Lite pitch fix
findings.text: GPU delegate latency (mean, correct runs only): VENTUNO Q 48.77 ms (468703, Mesa 25.1.8) to 30.58 ms; RB3 Gen 2 35.3 ms (469628, 469622) to 24.2 ms; IQ-9075 EVK 17.65 ms (469652, 469648) to 11.24 ms. The UNO Q runs on the GPU at about 330 ms (it had no working GPU path before 2026-10-04). Top-1 7/7 and cosine 1.0 against TensorFlow Lite on the CPU on every correct run.

findings.title: F19: the HTP power configuration no longer fails (fastrpc 1.0.8 RPC poll mode)
findings.text: No 'Failed to set powerConfig with error 0x32ce' in any QNN HTP run. HTP latency: IQ-9075 EVK NSP0 1.86 to 1.74 ms and NSP1 1.96 to 1.70 ms; RB3 Gen 2 (v68, never affected) 0.70 ms. VENTUNO Q: the measured npu0 values (11.43 ms in 468560, 8.56 ms in 468703, a mean of 3.93 ms here) are async queue-inflated and do not show the NPU's speed; synchronously it takes 0.40 ms per inference (see the next finding).

findings.title: VENTUNO Q NPU latency in the inference test is async queue-inflated: the NPU itself takes 0.40 ms per inference
findings.text: On the v75 NSP qnn-net-run runs asynchronously through dspqueue and queues inputs ahead, so QNN's per-inference time includes the wait behind the earlier queued inferences. That is why the measured VENTUNO Q npu0 mean ranges from 1.81 to 8.09 ms with p90 up to 4.1 times p50 across this run's full plans. A FastRPC timing shim shows 560 async inferences finish in 0.35 to 0.37 s of wall-clock time while QNN's per-inference times sum to 3.7 to 4.1 s (470186, 470187). Run synchronously (qnn-net-run --synchronous), the same model takes 0.398 to 0.406 ms per inference on the VENTUNO Q (470190, 470191: mean 0.401 ms, p50 0.400, p90 0.406), faster than the IQ-9075 EVK (1.74 ms) and the RB3 Gen 2 (0.70 ms), which do not run async (their sync and async numbers agree: 470203, 470347). The test's VENTUNO Q NPU numbers are therefore a measure of queue depth, not of the NPU, the kernel or the firmware. The fix (--synchronous in the inference test) is drafted, not yet applied.

findings.title: F20 again on ventunoq-matthart-production-01: GPU outputs are wrong after a GMU RPMh handshake loss at boot
findings.text: Both full plans that ran on this board in the first pass (BL2 469813, SPL 469826) fail gpu-tflite-gpu-top1 and -vs-cpu: every image classifies as one constant class (847 'tank' in 469813, 36 'terrapin' in 469826), not the all-zero output seen before. The console shows the F20 signature: 'HFI_H2F_MSG_PREPARE_SLUMBER id 7 timed out' at 5.4 s, then at the first GPU job 'Timeout waiting for GMU OOB set GPU_SET' and 'hangcheck detected gpu lockup', recovered. ventunoq-01 logged the same HFI timeout at boot (469819). The other VENTUNO Q boards are clean. Root cause still open (GPU RSC handshake through RPMh). The PMU reruns of the full plans all landed on other boards and passed the GPU cases; LAVA cannot exclude a board by tag.

findings.title: F8 is not intermittent: the RB3 Gen 2 policy4 minimum frequency always reads back wrong
findings.text: cpufreq-policy policy4-min fails in all four RB3 Gen 2 full plans of this run on three boards (469704 rb3g2-01, 469705 rb3g2-03, 470148 rb3g2-03, 470149 rb3g2-hyd-01) and in every RB3 Gen 2 full plan since 2026-10-03 (468564, 469619, 469622, 469628): 'policy4: set 691200 read 1651200' (1516800 in two runs). The timed busy loop shows the core does run at 691200 kHz (runtime ratio 3.40, 98 % of the frequency ratio), so the frequency change works and the value the kernel reports back is wrong. Eight failures in eight runs on four boards: a consistent readback bug, which earlier notes labelled a flake. Owner: Kodiak cpufreq readback (OSM/EPSS current-frequency path); not yet investigated.

findings.title: rb3g2-01 reaches userspace about 30 s later than the other RB3 Gen 2 boards
findings.text: On rb3g2-01 the kernel runs /init at 49.8 s (469704; also 51.5 s in 469623 and 47.7 s in 466642 on the same board) against 18.9 s on rb3g2-03. The console shows the Renesas xHCI on PCIe (0001:04:00.0) 'xHCI HW not ready after 5 sec (HC bug?) status = 0x1801', then 'Zeroing 64bit base registers, expecting fault', 23 s of silence and 'can't setup: -110'. The other boards print the same 'not ready' line with status 0x801 and continue. Board specific; root cause not established.

findings.title: Smaller initramfs on the RB3 Gen 2 and IQ-9075 EVK (the GPU stack's developer tools are trimmed on every board now)
findings.text: Moving the VENTUNO Q GPU stack onto qcom/gpu/gpu.mk applies its post-build trim to the Kodiak and Lemans images too: initramfs 174392K to 132544K (RB3 Gen 2) and 213860K to 172016K (IQ-9075 EVK). The IQ-9075 EVK frees the initrd at 3.0 s instead of 8.3 s and reaches the login prompt up to 8 s earlier (25.0 and 29.7 s against 33.8 and 29.1 s from XBL end). No test case changed.

findings.title: IQ-9075 EVK QNN CPU latency depends on the board (26.5 ms vs 45.6 ms)
findings.text: QNN CPU backend mean 26.50 ms on rb8-hyd-03 (469795) and 45.65 ms on rb8-hyd-07 (469796); the earlier runs show the same split inside one run (p50 26.9 ms, p90 45.2 ms in 469652). TFLite XNNPACK on the CPU is 11.6 ms on both boards. Likely F13: without cpufreq the two clusters stay at their boot frequencies (about 1.6 GHz and 0.6 GHz measured on 2026-10-02), and the single-threaded QNN CPU run lands on either cluster. Not verified in this run.

findings.title: PMU overflow interrupts fixed on the VENTUNO Q and the RB3 Gen 2 (PPI partitions)
findings.text: The PMU PPI-partition device tree commits (queued for upstream review) were added to the board kernels and the affected jobs rerun with new kernel/rootfs fingerprints on this run's signed firmware. VENTUNO Q: kvm-unit-tests PMU 11/11 in all four full plans (BL2 470155, 470156; SPL 470157, 470158), against 6/11 in the superseded jobs; nothing else changed apart from the intermittents below. RB3 Gen 2: 8/11 in 470148 and 470149 (pmu-basic-event-count now passes; the three remaining failures vary from run to run, the KVM PMU emulation race at full A78 clock seen in 468546 and 468572). Host overflow probe: PMU interrupts equal the expected overflows on all eight CPUs of both boards (VQ 470143, RB3 Gen 2 470046); each PMU now serves only its cluster (VQ a55 cpus=0,5-7, a78 cpus=1-4; RB3 Gen 2 a55 0-3, a78 4-7). dtbs_check W=1 before and after: 0 new warnings (monaco 9 DTBs, kodiak 29 DTBs).

findings.text: RB3 Gen 2: 'psci: [Firmware Bug]: failed to set OSI mode: -3' and a login timeout (maxcpus=2, 4, 6, negative), and with maxcpus=1 'CPU4: will not boot' followed by 'PM: Reset by PSHOLD' and a RamDump load; the same as the 2026-10-02 runs. IQ-9075 EVK: silence after the EFI stub on all maxcpus values and the negative control, as in 466663 to 466667 (earlycon diagnostics then showed an SError in amba_read_periphid).

findings.title: UNO Q QNN CPU entry reported absent: QAIRT 2.42 does not support the QRB2210
findings.text: The UNO Q processing units are now cpu:tflite and gpu:tflite-gpu, with cpu-qnn in ABSENT. The QAIRT 2.42 CPU backend rejects soc_id 524 ('Could not initialize backend'); diag 469668 showed the same binary and model run the graph on the same Cortex-A53 cores when soc0/soc_id reads 675 or 497, and fail with 524. An external limitation of the SDK's SoC table, not a failure of the stack.

findings.title: Negative controls failed as designed
findings.text: VENTUNO Q BL2 470163 (PMU rerun; first pass 469824) and SPL 469827, UNO Q 469801: wrong fingerprints, wrong maxcpus value, no KVM, every NPU case down with the NSP stopped, every GPU case down without an OpenCL platform, every top-1 wrong with rotated classes. RB3 Gen 2 469706 and IQ-9075 EVK 469802 (inference negative controls): the same for the inference cases. No negative control passed where it must fail. The VENTUNO Q negative control differs from its baseline 469692 only because 469692 hit F7 (HTP session create 0x80000406 after the NSP restart) and this run did not.

findings.title: F7 showed twice in the VENTUNO Q PMU reruns; an A/B diagnostic does not tie it to the device tree change
findings.text: 470155 failed fastrpc cdsp-unsigned-pd and 470156 failed every NPU case (QNN HTP), both with 'ERROR 0x80000406: Unable to create FastRPC session on domain 3' at unsigned-PD session creation; 0 of 4 first-pass full plans hit it. A diagnostic of 30 unsigned-PD and 10 signed-PD session rounds per boot passed every round on both kernels and four boards (first-pass ESP 55 of 55 unsigned rounds, PMU ESP 46 of 46; two of the jobs stopped before their 30th round), so the change is not implicated. F7 stays an open intermittent. Not seen this run: F3 (DPU vblank WARN), F6 (poweroff hang), F18 (IQ-9075 EVK unsigned PD: 2 of 2 passed).

systemready.intro:
Arm SystemReady devicetree band ACS v3.1.2 (release v26.03_DT_3.1.2) with its Linux rebuilt on 7.3-rc5, run unattended in LAVA on this run's firmware: the ACS ESP and root filesystem are flashed to the board's efi and rootfs partitions, the devicetree is the one the open boot stack Linux boots with, installed as /dtb/<fdtfile> on the ESP (VENTUNO Q qcom/monaco-arduino-monza.dtb, as the U-Boot of this run names it; UNO Q qcom/qcm2290-arduino-imola.dtb; RB3 Gen 2 qcom/qcs6490-rb3gen2.dtb; IQ-9075 EVK qcom/lemans-evk.dtb). Every firmware banner of every reboot is checked for the build fingerprint.

The 2026-10-02 baselines (467326, 467551, 467373, 467554) ran firmware with the SystemReady fix set (U-Boot PMIC RTC and EFI SetTime, U-Boot network on the VENTUNO Q and IQ-9075 EVK, the RB3 Gen 2 APSS watchdog, the UFS zero-length command fix, the UNO Q QTimer frames and CPU_SUSPEND in TF-A, DT fixes for the EL2 timer and the GIC maintenance interrupt). None of these are in this run's stack, which integrates the inference and GPU work only. The verdicts below therefore track the state before those fixes (466718, 466719), and the RB3 Gen 2 and IQ-9075 EVK runs stop on the failures the fix set addresses or leaves open.

reproduce:
Everything below uses the repositories listed in section 7. Commits marked local, not yet published must be published first; until then this run cannot be rebuilt from public sources alone. In particular the PMU PPI-partition patches are carried in qcom-buildroot (local branch), the OP-TEE patches of the RB3 Gen 2 and IQ-9075 EVK and two Linux patches of the IQ-9075 EVK are applied by the build kit from patch files, and the VENTUNO Q OP-TEE (monaco-pas-v3) and U-Boot (ventuno-q-v3-fdtfile) branches are local.

  1. Workspace: repo init -u https://github.com/EmbeddedAndroid/qcom-manifest -b <branch> -m <board>.xml with the build project replaced by qcom-buildroot integration-20261004. The published ventuno-q-v3 branch has monaco.xml; the agatti.xml, kodiak.xml and lemans.xml pins of this run are on the local all-boards branch (local, not yet published). Toolchains: make toolchains (Arm GNU Toolchain 14.3.Rel1), in an Ubuntu 24.04 build container.
  2. VENTUNO Q: override OP-TEE with monaco-pas-v3 and U-Boot with ventuno-q-v3-fdtfile, then make all TZ_IMAGE=u-boot-spl BUILD_ID=<SPL ID> and make all BUILD_ID=<BL2 ID>, plus the efi variants with LINUX_CMDLINE="... maxcpus=N", memtest=4 and maxcpus=2 kvm-arm.mode=none. QTI-sign the TZ image with make tz-qti-sign.
  3. RB3 Gen 2: make all BUILD_ID=<ID> with the OP-TEE PAS patches applied, then make tz-qti-sign. IQ-9075 EVK: make bootimage efi with TEE_IMPL_VERSION, LOCALVERSION and TF_A_FLAGS=... BUILD_STRING set to the build ID.
  4. UNO Q: TF-A imola (PLAT=uno_q SPD=opteed BL2 and FIP with OP-TEE PLATFORM=qcom-agatti and U-Boot qcom_defconfig tfa-optee.config arduino-uno-q.config), the arduino/linux-qcom kernel with the PAS series, and an ESP made from the VENTUNO Q userspace with the UNO Q kernel modules. QTI-sign BL2.
  5. Package each board's qcomflash (stock boot binaries with tz, uefi and efi replaced) and generate the jobs from the plan: plans/open-boot-stack in test-definitions, one full job, one job per maxcpus value, memtest=4 and the negative control; the SystemReady job flashes the ACS ESP and root filesystem with the board's DTB as /dtb/<fdtfile> (VENTUNO Q: qcom/monaco-arduino-monza.dtb).
  6. Submit to LAVA and compare by differencing two runs' measurements (get_job_results with limit 2000).

The job generators are not published yet; the job definitions of this run are public in LAVA (every job link in section 7) and can be resubmitted after replacing the artifact URLs.

notes.lede: Integrated build of the open boot stack (TF-A, OP-TEE, U-Boot, Linux at EL2 with KVM, Buildroot) on four Qualcomm boards, with every firmware component freshly built and fingerprinted, run through the complete open-boot-stack test plan in LAVA: the full plan twice per target (and per boot flow on the VENTUNO Q), one job per maxcpus value, memtest, the negative controls, and the Arm SystemReady DT band ACS. This run integrates the fastrpc 1.0.8 RPC poll mode (F19), Adreno firmware and the GPU userspace for the RB3 Gen 2 and IQ-9075 EVK, Mesa 25.2.8 with the TensorFlow Lite pitch fix, and the UNO Q socinfo change. The VENTUNO Q and RB3 Gen 2 full plans, maxcpus jobs and KVM negative controls were rerun with the PMU PPI-partition device tree fix added to their kernels (same signed firmware); the first-pass jobs are kept as superseded.
